reviews.summary: Hands-on review of version 2024.2. It calls the release a worthwhile upgrade mainly for the physics automation: AutoPhysics turns rough keys into more plausible motion. Caveats: AutoPhysics was still alpha, blendshapes were limited, and the free tier can't export or be used commercially.

reviews.summary: Judged as a video-to-mocap tool, Cascadeur's capture lost energy and sometimes twisted or floated, with no finger tracking. Its editing and cleanup tools were the strongest in the test, and TATO recommends it for refining rough mocap from other tools.
reviews.note: Rated for the video-mocap use only. Cascadeur's core keyframe/physics product is not what this test measured.

reviews.summary: Hands-on test with one humanoid character. Cascadeur's auto-rig was only adequate, but AutoPosing added believable weight and balance, and its FBX export was the cleanest and most retarget-ready in the comparison. About 30 minutes for a 2-second custom clip. Treated as a separate category used alongside Tripo or Meshy.
reviews.note: StraySpark is a game studio that sells unrelated UE/Blender tools (MCP servers) and has its own affiliate programme. It has no stake in these products. One tester, no numeric scores.

cascadeur.notes: Current version 2026.2.3 (dated 2026-10-01 on the download page) runs on Windows, Mac and Linux. Licence types are Free, Indie, Pro, Teams and Educational. Cascadeur is mainly a keyframe/physics animation and mocap-cleanup tool rather than a video-mocap tool, so compare it on that job. We found no independent quantitative benchmark. Editorial coverage (CG Channel, Digital Production, Creative Bloq 2025.1 news) describes features and does not test them.

vendor_claims.claim: DeepMotion aims to be the largest AI-generated 3D animation platform. The homepage relies on testimonials (e.g. Corridor Digital) and partner logos and gives no measured figures.
Foot-locking modes (Auto/Always/Never/Grounding) and a motion-smoothing dial reduce gliding and jitter. The vendor notes that heavy smoothing can cost accuracy.

SayMotion 1.5 (text-to-motion) was trained on an expanded dataset of about 400k clips and supports inpainting and chained prompts. It is full-body humanoid only, as reported by CG Channel from vendor information.

strengths: browser-based, no hardware, many export formats
adequate for standard locomotion and gestures
weaknesses: struggles with complex motion; limb and torso twist

reviews.author: StraySpark
reviews.summary: Meshy's auto-rig was fast and clean on a standard humanoid, with a broader motion library than Tripo. Hip and pelvis weighting was off by 5-15 cm, causing foot-IK mismatch and sliding, and non-standard bone names needed manual remapping for UE 5.7. Judged good for prototypes, less so for shipping work. Tripo was named best end-to-end for indies.

ratings.note: Covers Meshy overall. 84% of reviews are 5-star and 3% 1-star. Recent reviews shown don't mention rigging or animation.
'Easy rigging and animations' appears as a pro tag 3 times. One user said rigging works poorly when the model isn't in T- or A-pose.

mentions.source: Epic Developer Community: 'Can anyone help me properly animate characters from Meshy?'
mentions.note: The user reports wonky motion after Meshy rig+animate. A reply blames limb orientation and pose and the limits of auto-rigging, and suggests in-engine fixes.

vendor_claims.claim: Auto-rig in under 30 seconds and upload to animated character in under 2 minutes. Supports humanoids, quadrupeds and stylised figures. The library is described as both '600+' and '100+' presets on the same page. The page says animation is free to try.

strengths: very fast one-click rig and preset library
weaknesses: hip/pelvis weighting errors leading to foot sliding
poor results if input isn't T- or A-pose
meshy.notes: Meshy is primarily a 3D generator, and user ratings mostly reflect generation, not animation. The brief says rigging is paid-only, but the vendor feature page currently says auto-rig and animate are free to try; plan gating is unconfirmed. Sketchfab searches found Meshy-generated meshes but none whose description credits Meshy for the rig or animation; several credit Mixamo instead. No verified Meshy animation example.

vendor_claims.claim: Press release (2026-09-29): browser tool turns an image or text into a textured, rigged, animated asset, including non-human forms (wings, tails, wheels). It advises users to check topology and deformation before production.

bake3d.notes: We found no independent review, user rating or community discussion. It is very new (press release September 2026). Not researched further, per the brief.

vendor_claims.claim: Automatic skeleton fitting with no weight painting, an Animate tool for walk and idle cycles, and Pro-tier video-to-animation and text-to-motion.

sloyd.notes: Search found a unite.ai review (several languages) that reportedly tried the auto-rig and animate options and called the tool fast but limited for detailed editing, with a restricted free tier. We did not open it, so it is not recorded as a review. Not researched further.

vendor_claims.claim: The Animation Generator offers Text to Motion (Unity's own model) and Video to Motion (Kinetix model) inside the editor. Video input should be one full-body person on a stable camera.

unity-ai.notes: Unity AI arrived in Unity 6.2 (CG Channel, 2025-08-19: https://www.cgchannel.com/?p=169508). It replaced Muse (retired 2025-10-01) and is paid via Unity Points. We found no independent hands-on review of the animation generator. GameFromScratch reviewed the older Muse Animate, which we did not open.

caveats: 1) We found no independent quantitative benchmark for any of these tools, such as joint error against optical capture or a published text-to-motion leaderboard. Academic validation papers test research or open-source systems, not DeepMotion, Rokoko Vision, Cascadeur or Meshy. All benchmark arrays are therefore empty. 2) Reddit blocks our fetcher (reddit.com, old.reddit.com and search.json all refused), so community sampling relied on the Reallusion, Blender Artists, Unity, Epic and OpenGameArt forums plus one mirrored r/gamedev thread. Mention counts are low (Cascadeur 5, DeepMotion 3, Rokoko Vision 3, Meshy 1) and many are 2022-2024. 3) We could not read YouTube pages (no description, date or chapters). Titles and channels were verified via oEmbed, but verdicts and timestamps for those comparison videos are unverified, so none were scored as reviews. 4) G2 and Capterra returned 403. Figures from them come from search snippets and are marked verified:false. 5) We found no Steam listing for Cascadeur. 6) All independent Rokoko Vision evidence predates the Vision 3.0 solver rebuild (July 2026). 7) Many 2026 'review' pages (tooliverse, aitoolsbox, wavespeed, mimem, uthana, 3dxdev, itechguides, fbpe mirrors) are aggregator, affiliate or competitor content and were excluded or flagged. 8) Our review ratings translate qualitative verdicts into the 0-100 rubric. None of the sources gave numeric scores except 3D Next (4.5/5, flagged non-independent).
